subject: language
intro: Hi, I'm Ms. Alvarez, 6th grade ELA. Let's plan a lesson on citing text evidence — the skill that shows up in every other lesson.

beats.narration: "Prove it" is what I say all year, so it becomes the title.
This standard asks students to cite evidence that supports analysis of what the text says explicitly and what it implies.
I focus on inference because that's where citing evidence really matters.
beats.text: Students will be able to cite specific text evidence to support an inference about a character and explain how the evidence supports it.

beats.narration: Inferring from a picture practices the skill without the reading load.
beats.text: Show a photo of a messy kitchen with a half-eaten cake. "What happened here? Prove it with details from the picture."

beats.narration: Thinking aloud about strong vs. weak quotes is the most valuable part.
beats.text: Model with a short story excerpt: make an inference about the character, find a quote, and use the sentence frame "The text says ___, which shows ___." Think aloud about why some quotes are stronger than others.

beats.narration: Ranking the quotes pushes them to evaluate evidence, not just find it.
beats.text: Partners read a new excerpt, make an inference about a character, and find two quotes. They rank their quotes from strongest to weakest and justify the ranking.

beats.narration: The sentence frame keeps the check focused on the skill.
beats.text: Write one inference about the character in today's story and support it with a quote using the sentence frame.

outro: Picture, model, practice, check. Now you plan yours.
